text:
anya: Quick thread after the design review: two alternate patterns for the compare view I want to capture here. 1) compact density table with legend row + summary pill, 2) card-stack compare where each model is a card you can pin. Thoughts?

tara: Card-stack is promising for readability on mobile. Cards let us surface pin and changelog inline. But desktop compare needs wide density; a toggle between "Compact" and "Card" could work.

sam: Implementation notes: compact table can reuse existing compare table code, just add a density prop. Summary pill idea still helps when badges overflow: show "2 metrics" button in the cell that expands a small popover. Will wire up with `aria-expanded` and focus trap.

mike: Copy nit: prefer "Pin version" over "Lock version". "Lock" feels permanent and scary. Also if we surface pin on top of the catalog detail, include a small timestamp and changelog link e.g. "Pinned: v1.3.2 — changes".

zoe: Accessibility: popovers must be reachable by keyboard and announce state. Suggest using an ARIA live region for the summary content: `div role=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\"`. Also badges need text alternatives, e.g. `span class=\"badge badge--latency\" aria-label=\"latency 18ms\"` so screen readers get the value.

anya: Good point. Also we discussed a legend row above the table. Instead of a static legend, how about a collapsible legend that stays visible when keyboard focus is on the table? That solves discoverability on touch and keyboard without occupying space permanently.

tara: UX detail: legend collapsed state shows icons + short labels separated by bullets, expanded state shows extended descriptions and example ranges (latency, throughput, mem). I'll include contrast-sized swatches and microcopy like "lower is better" where relevant.

sam: For responsive behavior: at <720px switch to cards. At 720-1000px show compact table with summary pills for overflow. We can compute which badges to hide by priority list coming from the server (customer-configurable).

mike: Make sure enterprise customers can pin at org level vs project level. UI should indicate scope: "Pinned (org): v1.3.2". Also add a rollback button to the pin modal in case customers change their mind quickly.

zoe: Accessibility checklist I'll add: keyboard nav order, visible focus rings, focus return after popover close, aria-labels for badges, high-contrast variants, and support for screen-reader-only changelog link.

anya: design-bot: can you upload two mocks? one for compact table + collapsible legend, one for card-stack mobile-first.
design-bot: Mock uploads: "catalog/compare_compact_v2" and "catalog/compare_cards_v1". Reviews requested.

tara: I'll mock the toggle control and the pin surface (top-right of catalog detail). For the pin modal, include a short changelog preview and a confirm button labeled "Pin version".

sam: Prototype work: I'll build the summary pill component with keyboard and touch handlers. Quick note: avoid hover-only affordances for badges.

mike: Also tweak badge copy: instead of single words, use label + value e.g. "latency: 18ms" in the legend and in expanded pills. Less ambiguity.

anya: Action items: tara mock toggle + pin modal, sam prototype summary pill + responsive breakpoints, zoe a11y checklist and sample aria snippets, mike to confirm org/project pin scoping with two customers. We'll sync next week.

mike: small question: should we show a small "Compare settings" gear for users to set which badges are visible by default? Could save screen real estate.

tara: I like that. Add a settings gear in the header that opens a modal with reorder/hide controls; will add to mock.

anya: Great. Closing this thread for now, we'll capture decisions in the design doc. :white_check_mark:
